text:
ops_maya: incident-bot -> PagerDuty fired: PD alert for reranker-service canary. saw surge in 504s and latency right after canary roll at 02:42 UTC. canary fraction 15%. tagging oncall.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC89412 triggered for policy 'canary-deploy-health'. Service: reranker-service.

pd-bot: PagerDuty page -> jen_oncall. https://pagerduty.example.com/INC89412

jen_oncall: acked. pulling dashboards and logs. initial glance: p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.8s for reranker endpoint /v1/rerank.

andre_backfill: i'm hopping on to help with traces and flame graphs. any change in model flavor or kernel?

ops_maya: canary used image tag sha-2026-06-rerank-cpu-opt. change includes a new batching path and a switch to a different memory pool allocator.

jen_oncall: tracing shows request queueing on canary pods, worker threads sitting in `alloc_pool::reserve` and then failing fast with `std::bad_alloc` before returning 504 to gateway. short requests ok, long multi-query batches fail.

andre_backfill: interesting. could be memory ballooning on batched path. how many replicas in canary?

ops_maya: canary pool = 3 pods. node memory footprints spiking to 95% before OOM killer on one host.

eva_cs: heads up from support: two mid-market customers reported reranker failures on batched scoring jobs starting 02:44 UTC. opened ticket CS-9912.

jen_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) halt canary traffic fraction to 0 2) scale canary down to 0 replicas 3) capture heap profiles. executing now.

ops_maya: running: `kubectl patch canary reranker-service -n prod --type merge -p '{"spec": {"traffic": 0}}'`

pd-bot: note: page acknowledged by jen_oncall.

andre_backfill: capturing heapdump from a failing pod: saved to /tmp/heap-rerank-02-43.hprof. looks like allocator arenas not being released between batches.

jen_oncall: gateway confirms new requests not routed to canary. existing backlog still draining and returning 504s. initiating rollback to sha-2026-05-rerank-stable.

ops_maya: please also reduce max batch size at gateway to prevent heavy batch assembly causing memory spikes. setting MAX_BATCH=32 for now.

jen_oncall: applied feature flag: `gateway-max-batch-size=32` via config service. will monitor.

pd-bot: INC89412 status updated: mitigation in progress (canary traffic halted, batch size reduced).

andre_backfill: rollback command queued: `kubectl set image deployment/reranker-service reranker=registry.redwood/sha-2026-05-rerank-stable -n prod`

jen_oncall: monitoring rollout. also note: adding temporary pod anti-affinity to avoid co-locating heavy canary pods.

ops_maya: good. dump of failing stacktrace attached:

```
[2026-07-07T02:44:12Z] ERROR reranker: batch_assemble: arena overflow: requested=8604872, available=5242880
 at /app/serving/memory_pool.cpp:212
 at /app/serving/batcher.cpp:87
```

andre_backfill: confirms allocator arena cap is 5MB per request; new batching path requests larger contiguous slices and pushes over cap. patch in PR #7120 relaxed check but exposed aggregator behavior under load.

jen_oncall: rollout to stable completed at 02:51 UTC. canary replicas terminated; prod stable now serving stable pool. p95 back to baseline ~140ms.

eva_cs: emailed customers with initial mitigation note and support ticket reference.

ops_maya: follow-ups: 1) revert or fix allocator change in PR #7120 2) add canary gating rule: disallow canary traffic >5% for endpoints with batched requests until memory smoke tests pass 3) add heap profiling alert when node mem >85% for these services.

andre_backfill: i'll open hotfix PR to cap per-batch contiguous alloc request and add unit tests for large-batch flows. assigning to sara for review.

jen_oncall: handing off to andre for daytime watch. i'll write incident notes: "canary caused memory arena overflow on batched reranker; mitigation: halted canary traffic, reduced batch size, rolled back image; customers notified; follow-up owner @andre_backfill"

pd-bot: INC89412 acknowledged by jen_oncall and assigned to andre_backfill for follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident INC89412 mitigated at 02:58 UTC (rollback & batch size cap). please file postmortem in 72 hours.

andre_backfill: will take postmortem. opening INC-89412 in incident tracker and scheduling incident review. thanks team. :thumbsup:

ops_maya: great coordination. closing slack loop unless further alerts. :white_check_mark:
